translations.literal: Third month: Prince of Ping'en Commandery Chongfu was advanced to Prince of Qiao; Summer Office Vice Minister Zong Chuke became co-equal Fengge Luantai Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Chongfu, prince of Ping'en commandery, was raised to prince of Qiao, and Zong Chuke, vice minister of the summer office, joined the council as co-equal chief minister.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，韋安石知納言事，李嶠知內史事。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Wei Anshi managed the affairs of the Director of Proclamations; Li Qiao managed the affairs of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth summer month Wei Anshi took charge of proclamations and Li Qiao took charge of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丙子，幸興泰宮六月，天官侍郎崔玄暐同鳳閣鸞台平章事；

translations.literal: bingzi: Visited Xingtai Palace. Sixth month: Palace Ministry Vice Minister Cui Xuanwei became co-equal Fengge Luantai Chief Minister;
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi she visited Xingtai Palace. In the sixth month Cui Xuanwei, vice minister of the palace ministry, joined the council as co-equal chief minister;

sentences.zh: 李嶠為國子祭酒，知政事如故。

translations.literal: Li Qiao became Rector of the Directorate of Education, managing affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiao was made rector of the Directorate of Education while retaining his seat in government.

sentences.zh: 七月丙戌，楊再思為內史。

translations.literal: Seventh month, bingxu: Yang Zaisi became Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu of the seventh month Yang Zaisi was appointed director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 甲午，至自興泰宮。

translations.literal: jiawu: Returned from Xingtai Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu she returned from Xingtai Palace.

sentences.zh: 宗楚客左授原州都督。

translations.literal: Zong Chuke was demoted to military governor of Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Chuke was demoted and sent to govern Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八月，姚元崇為司僕卿，知政事；

translations.literal: Eighth month: Yao Yuanchong became Director of Palace Studs, managing affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Yao Yuanchong was made director of palace studs and kept his seat in government;

sentences.zh: 韋安石檢校揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Wei Anshi was made acting governor-general of Yangzhou Metropolitan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Anshi was made acting governor-general of Yangzhou metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，秋官侍郎張柬之同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Autumn Office Vice Minister Zhang Jianzhi became co-equal Fengge Luantai Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth winter month Zhang Jianzhi, vice minister of the autumn office, joined the council as co-equal chief minister.

sentences.zh: 十一月，李嶠為地官尚書，張柬之為鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Li Qiao became Minister of Earth; Zhang Jianzhi became Fengge Luantai Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Li Qiao was made minister of earth and Zhang Jianzhi chief minister of Fengge and Luantai.

sentences.zh: 自九月至於是，日夜陰晦，大雨雪，都中人有饑凍死者，令官司開倉賑給。

translations.literal: From the ninth month until now, day and night were overcast; great rain and snow fell; in the capital some died of hunger and cold; the offices were ordered to open granaries for relief.
translations.idiomatic: From the ninth month until now the skies stayed dark; heavy snow and rain fell; in the capital some froze or starved; the court ordered the granaries opened for relief.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年春正月，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: First year of Shenlong, spring first month: Great amnesty; changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong, on the first spring month, she proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 上不豫，制自文明元年已後得罪人，除揚、豫、博三州及諸逆魁首，咸赦除之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was unwell; an edict from the era of Civil Exaltation onward, for those convicted of crime—except the three prefectures of Yang, Yu, and Bo and the chiefs of various rebellions—all were pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor fell ill; she decreed that from the era of Civil Exaltation onward all the condemned—save the three prefectures of Yang, Yu, and Bo and the ringleaders of rebellion—were pardoned and released.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，麟台監張易之與弟司僕卿昌宗反，皇太子率左右羽林軍桓彥範、敬暉等，以羽林兵入禁中誅之。

translations.literal: guhai: Lintai Director Zhang Yizhi and his brother, Director of Palace Studs Changzong, rebelled; the Crown Prince led the Left and Right Forest Guards, Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, and others, entering the forbidden precinct with forest troops to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: On guhai Zhang Yizhi, director of Lintai, and his brother Changzong, director of palace studs, rose in rebellion; the crown prince led the left and right forest guards—Huan Yanfan, Jing Hui, and others—into the inner palace with armored troops and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，皇太子監國，總統萬機，大赦天下。

translations.literal: jiazi: The Crown Prince supervised the state, presiding over the myriad affairs; great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the crown prince assumed regency over all affairs of state and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 是日，上傳皇帝位於皇太子，徙居上陽宮。

translations.literal: That day the Emperor transmitted the imperial throne to the Crown Prince and moved to Shangyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the Emperor abdicated in favor of the crown prince and withdrew to Shangyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 戊申，皇帝上尊號曰則天大聖皇帝。

translations.literal: wushen: The Emperor was honored with the title August Emperor Zetian the Great Sage.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the Emperor was honored as August Emperor Zetian the Great Sage.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月壬寅，則天將大漸，遺制祔廟、歸陵，令去帝號，稱則天大聖皇后；

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, renyin: Zetian was near death; her final edict ordered enshrinement in the temple and burial in the mausoleum, and commanded that the imperial title be removed—she was to be called Empress Zetian the Great Sage;
translations.idiomatic: On renyin of the eleventh winter month Zetian was failing; her testament ordered temple enshrinement and burial in the imperial tomb, and stripped away the title of emperor—she was to be styled Empress Zetian the Great Sage;

sentences.zh: 其王、蕭二家及褚遂良、韓瑗等子孫親屬當時緣累者，咸令復業。

translations.literal: the Wang and Xiao families and the sons and grandsons and kin of Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, and others who had been implicated at the time—all were ordered restored to their professions.
translations.idiomatic: the Wang and Xiao clans and the sons, grandsons, and kin of Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, and others implicated in those days were all ordered restored to their professions.

sentences.zh: 是日，崩于上陽宮之仙居殿，年八十三，諡曰則天大聖皇后。

translations.literal: That day she died in the Hall of Immortal Dwelling at Shangyang Palace, aged eighty-three; posthumous title Empress Zetian the Great Sage.
translations.idiomatic: That day she died in the Hall of Immortal Dwelling at Shangyang Palace, aged eighty-three; her posthumous title was Empress Zetian the Great Sage.

sentences.zh: 二年五月庚申，祔葬於乾陵。

translations.literal: Second year, fifth month, gengshen: Enshrined and buried at Qianling.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen of the fifth month of the second year she was enshrined and buried at Qianling.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，詔依上元年故事，號為天后，未幾，追尊為大聖天后，改號為則天皇太后。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, an edict followed the precedent of the first year of Shangyuan and styled her Empress of Heaven; before long she was posthumously honored as Great Sage Empress of Heaven, and the title was changed to Empress Dowager Zetian.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong ascended, an edict following the Shangyuan precedent styled her Empress of Heaven; soon she was posthumously honored Great Sage Empress of Heaven, then retitled Empress Dowager Zetian.

sentences.zh: 太后嘗召文學之士周思茂、範履冰、衛敬業，令撰《玄覽》及《古今內範》各百卷，《青宮紀要》、《少陽政範》各三十卷，《維城典訓》、《鳳樓新誡》、《孝子列女傳》各二十卷，《內軌要略》、《樂書要錄》各十卷，《百僚新誡》、《兆人本業》各五卷，《臣範》兩卷，《垂拱格》四卷，並文集一百二十卷，藏于秘閣。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager once summoned literary scholars Zhou Simao, Fan Lübing, and Wei Jingye and ordered them to compile the Mysterious Overview and the Inner Canon of Past and Present, each one hundred scrolls; the Essentials of the Eastern Palace and the Standards of the Young Yang, each thirty scrolls; the Canon of the Moated City and the New Admonitions of the Phoenix Tower, the Biographies of Filial Sons and Exemplary Women, each twenty scrolls; the Essentials of Inner Rule and the Essentials of Music, each ten scrolls; the New Admonitions for the Hundred Officials and the Basic Occupations of the Myriad People, each five scrolls; the Model for Ministers in two scrolls; the Chuihong Regulations in four scrolls, and collected writings in one hundred twenty scrolls—all stored in the secret archive.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager once summoned the scholars Zhou Simao, Fan Lübing, and Wei Jingye and ordered them to compile the Mysterious Overview and the Inner Canon of Past and Present at one hundred scrolls each; the Essentials of the Eastern Palace and the Standards of the Young Yang at thirty each; the Canon of the Moated City, the New Admonitions of the Phoenix Tower, and the Biographies of Filial Sons and Exemplary Women at twenty each; the Essentials of Inner Rule and the Essentials of Music at ten each; the New Admonitions for the Hundred Officials and the Basic Occupations of the Myriad People at five each; the Model for Ministers in two scrolls; the Chuihong Regulations in four; and her collected writings in one hundred twenty scrolls—all lodged in the secret archive.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：治亂，時也，存亡，勢也。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Order and disorder depend on the age; survival and perishing depend on circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Whether the age is ordered or chaotic depends on the times; whether a house survives or falls depends on circumstance.

sentences.zh: 使桀、紂在上，雖十堯不能治；

translations.literal: Had Jie and Zhou been above, even ten Yao could not have governed;
translations.idiomatic: Had Jie and Zhou held the throne, even ten Yao could not have brought order;

sentences.zh: 使堯、舜在上，雖十桀不能亂；

translations.literal: had Yao and Shun been above, even ten Jie could not have thrown it into chaos;
translations.idiomatic: had Yao and Shun held it, even ten Jie could not have thrown the realm into chaos;

sentences.zh: 使懦夫女子乘時得勢，亦足坐制群生之命，肆行不義之威。

translations.literal: let a cowardly man or a woman seize the moment and gain power, and it is enough to sit and command the lives of the multitude and wantonly wield unrighteous might.
translations.idiomatic: let a timid man or a woman seize the moment and gain power, and it is enough to sit in command of every life and wield unrighteous might at will.

sentences.zh: 觀夫武氏稱制之年，英才接軫，靡不痛心于家索，扼腕于朝危，竟不能報先帝之恩，衛吾君之子。

translations.literal: Consider the years when the Wu clan held power: men of talent came in unbroken succession, yet none failed to grieve at the ruin of their houses and clench their fists at the court's peril—still they could not repay the former emperor's grace or defend their lord's son.
translations.idiomatic: In the years of Wu's rule, talent crowded the court in endless file, yet all grieved for ruined houses and clenched their fists at a court in peril—still they could not repay the late emperor's grace or defend their sovereign's son.

sentences.zh: 俄至無辜被陷，引頸就誅，天地為籠，去將安所？

translations.literal: Soon the innocent were trapped; they stretched their necks to the execution—Heaven and Earth became a cage; whither could they flee?
translations.idiomatic: Soon the innocent were trapped, necks offered to the blade—Heaven and Earth themselves were the cage; where could they flee?

sentences.zh: 悲夫！

translations.literal: Lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: How lamentable!

sentences.zh: 昔掩鼻之讒，古稱其毒；

translations.literal: In antiquity the slander of the nose-covering was called poisonous;
translations.idiomatic: The old tale of the nose-covering slander was called poison itself;

sentences.zh: 人彘之酷，世以為冤。

translations.literal: the cruelty of the human pig the world held as wrongful.
translations.idiomatic: the horror of the Human Pig the world counted as a crying wrong.

sentences.zh: 武后奪嫡之謀也，振喉絕繈褓之兒，菹醢碎椒塗之骨，其不道也甚矣，亦奸人妒婦之恆態也。

translations.literal: In the empress's plot to seize the succession she silenced infants still in swaddling clothes and minced the bones of consorts of the peppered chambers—her impiety was extreme, yet also the constant manner of jealous wicked women.
translations.idiomatic: In her bid for the throne she strangled babes in their wraps and ground the bones of rival consorts to paste—wicked beyond measure, yet the old habit of a jealous, vicious woman.

sentences.zh: 然猶泛延讜議，時禮正人。

translations.literal: Yet she still broadly extended frank counsel and at times honored upright men.
translations.idiomatic: Still she kept frank counsel in circulation and at times paid honor to upright men.

sentences.zh: 初雖牝雞司晨，終能復子明辟，飛語辯元忠之罪，善言慰仁傑之心，尊時憲而抑幸臣，聽忠言而誅酷吏。

translations.literal: Though at first a hen crowed at dawn, in the end she restored her son and clarified the throne; she refuted flying slander to clear Yuan Zhong's guilt, spoke kindly to comfort Ren Jie's heart, exalted the statutes of the age and checked favored ministers, heard loyal words and executed cruel officials.
translations.idiomatic: Though at first the hen ruled the dawn, in the end she restored her son and set the throne in order; she answered slander to clear Yuan Zhong, soothed Ren Jie with gracious words, exalted the law of the time and reined in favorites, heeded loyal counsel and put cruel officers to death.

sentences.zh: 有旨哉，有旨哉！

translations.literal: How apt—how apt!
translations.idiomatic: There is truth in this—truth indeed!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：龍漦易貌，丙殿昌儲。

translations.literal: [Eulogy] The eulogy says: Dragon seed changed face; the eastern palace flourished with an heir.
translations.idiomatic: 【Eulogy】 The eulogy says: Dragon seed took another face; the eastern palace swelled with heirs.

sentences.zh: 胡為穹昊，生此夔魖？

translations.literal: Why did the vault of Heaven bear this one-legged demon?
translations.idiomatic: Why did Heaven above breed this ogre and goblin?

sentences.zh: 奪攘神器，穢褻皇居。

translations.literal: She seized the sacred regalia and defiled the imperial residence.
translations.idiomatic: She snatched the sacred vessel and fouled the imperial halls.

sentences.zh: 窮妖白首，降鑒何如。

translations.literal: Evil pursued to white-haired old age—what judgment will Heaven send down?
translations.idiomatic: Her demonry ran to a white-haired end—what verdict will Heaven hand down?
